slides.title: Follow the ownership boundary
slides.takeaway: Library: Panel structure, resize interaction, visibility and empty-state primitives.
slides.notes: The library owns Panel structure, resize interaction, visibility and empty-state primitives. The host owns Content, search, durable width storage and feature actions.  The arrows show data/callback direction, not an implicit network request. The documented isolation rules and known implementation deviations are listed in qa-report.md.

cards.title: Logical placement
cards.body: SidebarOrientation selects the desired panel side.

cards.title: Header slots
cards.body: leftActions and rightActions are public API slot names.

cards.title: Width bounds
cards.body: defaultWidth, minWidth and maxWidth configure resizing.

slides.notes: Customization comes from the current exports and prop declarations. Logical placement: SidebarOrientation selects the desired panel side. Header slots: leftActions and rightActions are public API slot names. Width bounds: defaultWidth, minWidth and maxWidth configure resizing. For UI, import the package stylesheet and use documented props or stable public classes. A component-level color override and inherited theme tokens are different levels of control. Locale strings and direction should be supplied by the host; do not introduce app i18n into a reusable library.

slides.title: Constraints that affect integration

cards.title: No built-in search
cards.body: Compose search in children or header actions.

cards.title: Persistence is external
cards.body: onResizeStop reports width; the host decides where to save it.

cards.title: Contextual visibility
cards.body: Keep the parent layout and isOpen state synchronized.

slides.notes: Review these constraints before choosing the library. No built-in search: Compose search in children or header actions. Persistence is external: onResizeStop reports width; the host decides where to save it. Contextual visibility: Keep the parent layout and isOpen state synchronized. The package is private in this snapshot. The presence of build/publish tooling is not evidence that a compatible release is available from a registry.
